category_title: Students with learning disabilities exhibiting low motivation, poor frustration tolerance, and resistance to academic demands
minimal_context: The student is participating in a whole-class lecture and guided questioning session about new material.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are going to go over the new material on the screen. Please look at the first slide and tell me what you see.

STUDENT: (Keeps head down, not looking at the instructor or the media on the screen.) I don't see anything.

TUTOR: You need to look at the screen to answer the question. What do you think it says?

STUDENT: I don't know. I don't want to read it.

TUTOR: Just give it a try and follow along with the rest of the class.

STUDENT: (Gets out of the seat and speaks loudly, interrupting the instruction) I said I don't know! This is too hard and I'm not doing it!

options.A: Break the reading task down into smaller chunks so the student can complete them during the lesson.
options.B: Follow through to ensure the student complies with the direction to read the screen, helping them if they do not do it independently.
options.C: Introduce materials and questions to improve the rate of successful student responses through oral or written practices.
options.D: Give the student an easier reading task while the rest of the class works on the main content on the screen.
